title: Omnichannel customer service strategy: A leader’s guide | Pylon
summary: Learn how to build an omnichannel customer service strategy that connects channels, preserves customer context, and helps support teams scale.
body_markdown:
B2B support teams handle multi-channel, multi-stakeholder conversations regularly. A customer asks for help with an integration issue via live chat, and then follows up with more details by email. A different stakeholder on the account then asks for a progress update on Slack a few days later.


If the team uses fragmented systems or siloed inboxes, they’ll waste time searching for context and have to ask customers to repeat themselves, which gets frustrating quickly.


An omnichannel customer service strategy is meant to keep all those conversations connected and preserve context so that support teams can resolve issues efficiently, even as volume increases. This article defines what omnichannel support is and outlines six steps to help you build a connected strategy.


## What’s omnichannel customer service?


Omnichannel customer service (or customer support) connects all your communication channels to create a unified,[consistent customer experience](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/omnichannel-cx) .


As conversations move between a large number of channels (like email,[live chat](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/omnichannel-chat-definition-benefits-best-practices) , SMS, social media, Slack, and Microsoft Teams), an omnichannel approach helps the support team manage them all from a centralized workspace. Instead of constantly having to switch channels or start from scratch with every ticket, they have access to every part of a customer’s context for faster, more accurate responses.


[Omnichannel customer support](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/omnichannel-customer-support-definition-examples-strategy) is different from multichannel customer support. Multichannel support simply involves offering several separate channels, while omnichannel support connects them into a unified customer journey.


Chat integrations view from Pylon


## Why growing support teams need an omnichannel strategy


When a company is just starting out and only has a few customers, it’s easy to stay on top of messages in an email inbox and mentally keep track of that context when the conversation picks up on Slack or live chat.


As a company grows, fragmented channels become hard to manage, particularly for B2B teams who work with accounts that have multiple stakeholders. According to a[2026 McKinsey & Company study](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/the-surprising-economics-of-b2b-growth-the-new-survival-threshold-and-what-it-takes-to-thrive) , B2B customers use an average of 10 different channels throughout their customer journey, and 73% expect consistent experiences across every touchpoint.


It can be very difficult to efficiently manage that many channels without a dedicated omnichannel customer service strategy. When your communication strategy isn’t working, issues fall through the cracks as volume and complexity grow. Work is duplicated, team members spend more time looking for information, and handoffs are fraught, which all mean tickets take longer to resolve.


Here are the main benefits of[omnichannel support for B2B companies](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/practical-guide-to-omnichannel-support) :


- **Faster responses and resolutions.** With a coordinated communication strategy, your team gives customers faster response and resolution times.
- **Less repetition and fewer unnecessary handoffs.** Teams are less likely to duplicate work, and customers don’t have to repeat the same questions as often. Because everyone has access to the context they need, there’s less need for escalations, so first contact resolution rates rise.
- **More consistent customer experiences.** When every conversation is managed in one place, customers get consistent answers across all channels, leading to better experiences and higher[customer satisfaction scores (CSATs)](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/customer-satisfaction-score) .
- **Better team efficiency and collaboration.** Cross-team collaboration is easier when everyone has access to the same shared context instead of working in silos.
- **Greater visibility into customer journeys and account health.** A strong[omnichannel support platform](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/omnichannel-support-platforms) gives you analytics and insights to identify churn risk, so you can intervene to preserve customer relationships and retention.


## 6 steps to build a connected support strategy


Follow these six steps for an omnichannel customer service strategy that gives customers a more connected, consistent experience across channels:


1. **Map the customer journey.** Start by identifying the channels customers actually use. Build a map of important channels and touchpoints at each stage of the customer lifecycle, and focus your efforts on the channels that your customers value most. For example, email is better for longer, more detailed messages, while Slack and live chat are good for troubleshooting in real time.
2. **Prioritize channels and set up connections.** Choose high-volume and high-value channels you want to focus on first. Then, connect them to an omnichannel support platform to link recent conversations to the account’s broader context.
3. **Define ownership, routing, and handoff and escalation procedures.** Create workflows that allow customers to switch channels without restarting the conversation. Use automations and AI agents to help your team follow consistent processes when work moves to a different channel or needs to be passed to another team.
4. **Integrate tools.** The more integrated your systems are, the more context your team can preserve. Connect your support platform to your CRM, billing, issue tracking, and collaboration tools to reduce silos and help teams share information. If you’re using AI agents or[conversational AI tools](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/conversational-ai-customer-service-platforms) , give them access to the context they need to find data and resolve problems.
5. **Establish consistent service standards.** Set targets for key metrics like response and resolution times, as well as service quality and CSAT. Then, train your team on cross-channel workflows so they can meet these standards consistently.
6. **Track the right metrics.** Set up an analytics dashboard that shows you real-time changes in first response time (FRT), time to resolution (TTR), first contact resolution (FCR), CSAT, ticket volume, and customer retention. Look for bottlenecks to find where you still need to improve processes, and optimize your strategy over time.


## Omnichannel customer service in action


Issue view from Pylon


Here are a couple of real-world examples to show what omnichannel communication is like in practice.


B2B tech startup[Vellum](https://www.usepylon.com/case-study/vellum) used hundreds of Slack channels to communicate with customers, but problems mounted as the company grew. Vellum’s customer support team had no way to assign issues to specific team members or track resolution and response times, and giving customers a product update meant pasting the same message in every channel individually.


Vellum solved these problems by centralizing its Slack and live chat conversations into Pylon’s centralized platform. The team can now assign and track issues through to completion while getting detailed metrics and automated alerts about service-level agreement (SLA) breaches.


Meanwhile,[Lightdash](https://www.usepylon.com/case-study/lightdash) was using separate apps to manage conversations via email, in-app chat, Slack Connect, and Slack Community. Adopting Pylon’s omnichannel support platform meant the team can now coordinate conversations on all four channels from one place. Team members use assignment and private notes to collaborate, and can view context from their CRM to give more accurate, relevant responses.

## FAQ


### Is omnichannel customer service only for large companies?


No. Mid-sized and small teams can also create an omnichannel experience for their customers when they communicate across several channels. You don’t have to adopt a full-scale solution at once; scope and technology can scale with the support operation’s complexity.


### How long does it take to implement an omnichannel customer service strategy?


It depends. Timelines vary based on the number of channels, integrations, existing systems, and workflow complexity. A phased rollout can help teams introduce omnichannel support gradually.


### How does omnichannel support affect customer retention?


A more consistent and convenient support experience can reduce friction or negative sentiments and strengthen satisfaction and loyalty, which can support long-term retention efforts.


### Can omnichannel customer service reduce support costs?


An omnichannel customer support approach can help teams operate more efficiently by reducing duplicate work and improving agent productivity, so you can simplify headcount without sacrificing quality.


### How do you maintain data privacy across omnichannel support?


It comes down to the integrations and ways you connect each channel and platform to the main omnichannel tool. Teams should use appropriate access controls, data governance, and security policies within a compliant system to protect customer information.
